name: Street Custom 'Sunday School' Weaponized Religious Artifact
description: A broad category of improvised weapons concealed within or fabricated from religious objects — crucifixes with hidden blades, prayer beads strung with ball bearings for use as a flail, hollowed scripture books containing pistols, incense burners filled with chemical agents, and ceremonial staffs weighted with lead cores. Sunday School weapons have proliferated in GLMZ's religious communities where faith and survival intersect. The weapons exploit a cultural reluctance to search religious items at checkpoints and social gatherings, turning devotional objects into a delivery system for violence. The practice is controversial within the communities that produce it — some see it as sacrilege, others as the ultimate expression of a faith tested by circumstance.
specifications:
type: Variable — bladed crucifixes, weighted prayer beads, gun-books, chemical incense
concealment: Within culturally protected religious objects
effectiveness: Variable by specific build
detection: Low — cultural reluctance to search religious items
cost: Φ20-500 depending on complexity
construction: Ranges from crude modifications to skilled craft work
story_hooks: A religious leader was assassinated with a blade concealed in a ceremonial cross — the weapon was handed to them by a congregant during a ritual and the killing was committed in front of hundreds.

A checkpoint security team has begun searching religious items, provoking a community uprising over cultural desecration — but they keep finding weapons, validating the searches they should not be performing.

physical_description.visual_profile: A worn wooden crucifix approximately 30cm tall, traditional Christian iconography with darkened brass accents. At first glance, indistinguishable from a devotional object found in any GLMZ chapel or home shrine. The corpus figure shows careful hand-carving; the crossbeam and vertical post exhibit subtle reinforcement beneath aged finish. Weight distribution feels deliberately unbalanced—heavier toward the base than authentic religious pieces.
physical_description.dimensions: Height: 28-32cm | Width: 16-18cm | Depth: 2-3cm | Hidden blade cavity: 12-15cm length, recessed 0.8cm into crossbeam
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively heavy for its size—approximately 800-1100 grams. Feels substantial in palm, not fragile like museum pieces. The weight settles unnaturally low, suggesting concealed material. A trained hand recognizes the density is wrong.
physical_description.primary_material: Outer: aged oak or reclaimed wood (darkened with stain). Inner reinforcement: steel leaf spring or surgical steel blade folded into crossbeam cavity. Brass ferrule and mounting hardware show legitimate patina.
physical_description.finish: Weathered natural wood with dark walnut stain. Brass accents exhibit genuine verdigris and oxidation. Carved corpus shows hand-tool marks consistent with street craftwork—not machine-precise. Surface appears genuinely aged, with micro-scratches and lacquer wear from years of devotional handling.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep brown-black wood body | Oxidized green-brass accents | Pale bone or resin corpus figure | Hidden steel blade reveals dull gunmetal when deployed
physical_description.grip_texture: Smooth worn wood, slightly tacky from years of handling oils and incense residue. The vertical post tapers slightly for palm grip. Brass cross-guard provides texture break. No intentional grip enhancement—authenticity maintained.
distinctive_features: Hairline seam running along one side of crossbeam where blade cavity is sealed
Brass mounting hardware shows file marks from field modification
Corpus figure's hands positioned to obscure blade release mechanism
Faint prayer inscriptions etched into rear face—genuine devotional text or camouflage unclear
Small brass hinge concealed within right arm socket—hint of mechanical integration
Scent of old incense permanently absorbed into wood grain
Minor burn marks on base suggesting use in actual religious ceremonies
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: No corporate branding. Hand-carved initials or prayer abbreviations on rear: possibly 'S.S.' (Street Smith) or religious notation in Aramaic/Latin. Unmarked to maintain plausible deniability as authentic artifact.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn but meticulously maintained. Shows genuine age patina but no obvious damage. The contradiction—too pristine to be truly centuries old, too weathered to be new—creates uncanny valley effect. Scratches appear from actual use in religious practice, not combat. Some examples show deliberate scuff-marks added during fabrication to increase authenticity.
